entities.summary: Curtis Lester Patrick was a Canadian professional ice hockey player and coach associated with the Victoria Aristocrats/Cougars of the Pacific Coast Hockey Association, and the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League (NHL). Along with his brother Frank Patrick and father Joseph Patrick, he founded the PCHA and helped develop several rules for the game of hockey. Patrick won the Stanley Cup six times as a player, coach and manager. Lester Patrick was a athletes & competitors from Drummondville (1883-12-30, Drummondville–1960-06-01). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lester Patrick's contributions to hockey helped shape the sport in North America, with his six Stanley Cup wins as a player, coach, and manager having a lasting impact on the game. His involvement in founding the PCHA also laid groundwork for the NHL.
